Reduced motion stops the terminal's blink attribute (rich-animation-42lg.xbt)

A reduced-motion console still wrote SGR 5 for `[blink]`, which the
terminal animates on its own. The reader's preference now lives on
`Destination` (`reducedMotion`), resolved once by `resolveDestination`;
each host's `RenderOptions.reducedMotion` reads it back from there.
`shownOn` unsets blink and blink2 (`Style.reduced()`) for the one encoder
and for a recording console, so print, Live/App frames, renderToString
and the HTML/SVG/text exports all show the text steady. Drawing could not
do it: the console lays its print and base styles on after render.

A lifecycle arrives and leaves through a glyph transition too (rich-animation-42lg.s91) (#496)

* A lifecycle arrives and leaves through a glyph transition too (rich-animation-42lg.s91)

* A glyph exit ends at nothing: backspace and scrambleOut (rich-animation-42lg.s91)

/code-review high: typewriter and scramble only resolve toward the text, so
offered as an exit they replayed the arrival — a jump to scrambled at
`left`, the text reassembling, then gone. The glyph catalogue gains the two
ways out, each whole at 0 and blank at its seconds, and the test now samples
the whole exit and pins that it never gives a glyph back.

`key` names the element, so it is the lifecycle's again, once for both
halves; a theme stays on the colour half, the only one with a ground.
Not taken: `onBeat` over a lifted half is a compile error, not a silent one,
and the docs apply it before lifting.

* The glyph ways out join the catalogue; scrambleOut keeps a glyph no cell wide (rich-animation-42lg.s91)

/code-review medium: scrambleOut read an unplaced cell as -1, behind its
blanking front from t=0, so a zero-width glyph was dropped before the element
began to leave. An unplaced cell is now beyond both fronts. And the docs named
backspace and scrambleOut catalogue members while the catalogue did not hold
them; it does now, as the colour catalogue holds dissolve, so templates spell
them and the glyph-effects demo shows them.
